summary.added_external_crate_count_note: P2-N8 admits no external crate. academic-what-if links academic-critical-path, academic-curriculum, academic-domain, academic-offering, academic-proposal, academic-record, academic-review, academic-scenario, serde, sha2 and thiserror as product edges, and those eight workspace packages again plus academic-ingestion, academic-model-run, serde_json and trybuild as dev edges, all covered by earlier reviewed receipts, and adds one workspace path package. Nothing links into a product binary that was not already there: the eight workspace product edges are path packages this repository already builds, and serde, sha2 and thiserror were admitted by the phase 1 receipt. Build-time-only additions are zero -- there is no build script, no proc macro beyond serde's and thiserror's, and no code generator. The crate declares no binary target and no example target.
summary.added_workspace_path_package_note: academic-what-if is the P2-N8 boundary: section 22's what-if semester simulator. It owns the PlanScenario of section 22.1, the hard split between section 22.2's seven deterministic results and section 22.3's seven projections in both the data type and the UI section, the STALE_INPUT marking that freezes a plan and the consent that unfreezes it, the section 22.4 comparison that produces no aggregate recommendation score and explains a reordering, and the end-of-term calibration whose subject is the model. It is a separate package from academic-scenario because that crate owns the projected/actual type isolation and links only academic-domain, and giving it seven more product edges would have widened the closure a projected value is sealed inside; it is a separate package from academic-critical-path, academic-offering and academic-audit because it reads all three rather than deciding anything any of them decides. It registers no deterministic engine: section 28's table has twelve rows, the P2-C5 registry is pinned to that table as an enumeration, and none of the twelve is a semester simulator, so this crate claims no engine_id and adds nothing under testdata/engines/.

no_second_ladder_note: Section 22.3's ProjectedEvidenceOpportunity, its three opportunity kinds, its four likelihood bands and its four opportunity bases were fixed by P2-C7, and this crate declares no second future-knowledge vocabulary: sections 22.3's first three bullets are that crate's ScenarioProjection verbatim, produced by that crate's own project, and every band this crate carries is that crate's LikelihoodBand. Section 29.5's six bias dimensions were fixed by P2-U8 and a projected workload takes one BiasDisclosure by value rather than restating them; the four facets section 22.4 names are four of those six, parsed out of the design document and mapped in both directions. Section 16.4's four path roles were fixed by P2-N6 and the path-coverage projection reads CriticalPathResult::roles rather than computing a path. Section 8.3's four offering standings were fixed by P2-U5 and the deterministic lane takes ConfirmedSeat values, whose one producer is ConfirmedStanding::seat, so a HISTORICALLY_LIKELY offering has no seat to hand it. Section 10's grade table and repeat policy were fixed by P2-U4 and a stated-grade GPA scenario is read through that crate's own versioned GradingScheme at that scheme's own published scale. Section 27.4's user decision was fixed by P2-M2 and the recomputation consent takes a UserDecision, whose one producer refuses every actor that is not a user. Section 11's graduation verdict was fixed by P2-U3 and this crate cannot reach it at all: academic-audit is absent from its declared closure of every kind, and a compile-fail case proves that academic_audit:: is not a path that resolves here. The counts section 22 fixes -- four basedOn keys, six PlanScenario keys, three assumptions, seven deterministic bullets, seven projected bullets, six comparison dimensions, three staleness causes -- are each measured against the design document in both directions rather than restated as numbers, and one reading the document leaves open is recorded with a test that fails when it stops saying so: section 22.4's 후속 경로 row is labelled Mixed because section 22 puts its official-unlock half in 22.2 and its informal-readiness half in 22.3.

direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-critical-path: P2-N6's CriticalPathResult and PathRole. Section 22.3's sixth bullet is Critical Path coverage 가능성, and this crate computes no path: PathCoverageTargets::from_critical_path reads that engine's own role assignment and the coverage projection is an overlap between those concepts and the published material of the plan's choices. The edge is what keeps this crate from holding a second notion of what is on a path.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-curriculum: P2-U1's Credits, CurriculumCategory, Meeting, Weekday and OfficialPrerequisite. Section 22.2's first, second, third and fifth bullets are about a catalogue row's credits, an official timetable, an official prerequisite and a category allocation, and all five types are that crate's. Meeting's half-open minute range is that crate's own reading of section 8.2 and the overlap rule here reuses it rather than restating it.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-domain: EntityId, CourseId, OfferingId, ModelRunId, ContentDigest, TimestampMillis and Decimal. Every identifier a plan names, the digests section 22.1's basedOn block references, the instants it compares, and the fixed-point value a GPA scenario is expressed in.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-offering: P2-U5's ConfirmedSeat and CancellationNotice. The seat is the only value in this workspace that carries a real timetable, and its one producer is ConfirmedStanding::seat, so section 8.3's placeholder만, 졸업계획 확정에 사용 금지 reaches the deterministic lane as an argument that cannot be supplied rather than as a check. The notice is section 22.5's 폐강 half of the staleness rule, already refused by that crate for every source level that does not publish offering changes.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-proposal: P2-M2's UserDecision. Section 22.5 asks for 재계산 동의, and that type's one producer refuses a deterministic engine, a model run and an importer by name, so a background job that recomputed a stale plan on its own is a call with no argument to make.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-record: P2-U4's GradingScheme, GradeSymbol and the fixed-point decimal arithmetic. Section 22.2 admits a GPA scenario only under grades the user stated, and the table those grades are read through is that crate's versioned scheme rather than a second copy of section 10's table. What the edge does not bring is the record itself: this crate names no attempt, no ledger and no history, and a hypothetical term average is a different type from that crate's GpaValue with no conversion between them.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-review: P2-U8's BiasDisclosure. Section 22.4 requires a workload to be displayed with its sample count, its recency, its selection bias and its instructor and term mix, and that type's only producer names all six of section 29.5's dimensions, so a workload with no bias beside it is not a value this crate can build.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-scenario: P2-C7's whole projected lane: ScenarioProjection, ProjectedEvidenceOpportunity, LikelihoodBand, OpportunityBasis, OpportunityKind, Proposed, ProposalProvenance, ProjectedWorkloadRange, WorkloadHoursRange, ProjectionCalibration and project. This is the edge the task is built on: section 22.3's first three bullets are that crate's output unmodified, the workload proposal this crate seals is that crate's sealed wrapper, and the calibration direction vocabulary is that crate's, so there is one answer in this repository to what a projection may say about the future.

dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-critical-path: Declared a second time for the trybuild reason academic-scenario gives: a compile-fail case compiles against this crate plus this crate's dev-dependencies, and the acceptance suite builds a PathCoverageTargets from that engine's own role pairs.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-curriculum: The same, for the Meeting values two choices conflict on and the Credits and CurriculumCategory a catalogue row carries.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-domain: The same, for the identifiers and instants every fixture names, and for the whole Actor enumeration the consent test walks.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-ingestion: P2-U6's SourceCategory, which a P2-U5 official listing and a P2-U5 cancellation notice are built from. The suite drives that crate's own resolve rather than assembling a seat, because ConfirmedStanding::seat is the only producer of one in this workspace.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-model-run: P2-M1's CalibrationRegistry, which P2-U5's resolve takes by reference. The fixture passes no forecast policy, so no prediction runs and the standing is decided by the official registration-system reading alone.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-offering: Declared a second time for the trybuild reason, and for the corpus this suite reuses rather than transcribes.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-proposal: The same, for the UserDecision the consent test builds from each actor kind in turn.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-record: The same, for the GradeSymbol a stated grade names and the TermKey a seat carries.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-review: The same, for the BiasDisclosureDraft the fixture builds a six-dimension disclosure through.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-scenario: The same, for the SyllabusConceptSignal a choice carries and the WorkloadHoursRange it assumes.
dev_workspace_dependencies.serde_json: scenario_basis_round_trip drives a ScenarioBasis through a real encoder and compares the object's key set against BASIS_FIELDS in both directions, and workload_is_a_range_with_bias_metadata reads the sealed workload through P2-C7's own wire form, which is the only route out of that seal and the route that crate documents.
dev_workspace_dependencies.trybuild: The compile-fail suite. Nine cases under crates/what-if/tests/compile_fail assert that each refusal is a program that does not compile with a committed diagnostic: naming the canonical writer, naming P2-U3's determinate verdict, assembling a plan field by field, calling the deterministic lane's crate-private constructor, calling a rule contribution's crate-private producer, reading a point estimate off a projected workload, defaulting a comparison priority, recomputing a frozen plan without a consent, and assigning through a comparison's shared borrow.

why_this_dependency_belongs_inside_its_t: academic-what-if is a workspace path crate, not an external dependency. It owns section 22's simulator and, for each rule, the value that does not exist rather than the check somebody has to remember to run: it has no edge of any kind to academic-store or academic-store-platform, so the canonical writer is not nameable here and INV-C-009 is a fact about the dependency graph rather than a rule inside a function; DeterministicResults and ProjectedResults share no field, no constructor and no conversion, and SectionView's two arms borrow two different types, so a projection has no position under the deterministic heading; every value the engine produces has private fields and one crate-private producer, so a plan cannot be assembled to say something the engine did not compute; RuleContribution::under takes the hypothetical completion assumption by value and GpaScenario::under refuses a stated-grade set that leaves any choice unstated, so section 22.2's two conditions are arguments rather than flags; ProjectedWorkload takes a six-dimension BiasDisclosure by value and has no midpoint, mean or expected accessor, so a workload is a range with its bias and never a point; DimensionPriority is a complete permutation with no Default and no arithmetic combining two dimensions, so there is no aggregate recommendation score and no shipped neutral ordering; FrozenPlan returns its plan unchanged and FrozenPlan::recompute takes a consent built from a UserDecision, so a stale plan is frozen rather than corrected; and the crate spells no mastery word at all, which is how P2-N3 held section 1's fifth invariant and how it is held here. Its dependency set is minimal for a composition task and the edges it does not have are the point: no academic-store, so no plan reaches the canonical writer and no migration is added; no academic-audit of any edge kind, so the hypothetical graduation mode has no route to P2-U3's three-gate DETERMINATE rule; no academic-knowledge-state and no academic-ledger as direct edges; no academic-worker and no academic-egress-boundary as direct edges, so no product file here can launch a process or stage a payload; and no academic-model-run as a product edge, so nothing in the product path can call a model.
network_posture: The crate opens no socket, opens no file, reads no clock, declares no foreign function, reads no environment variable, spawns no process, and runs no build script. It takes no mutable borrow of anything and holds no interior mutability of any kind: plan_scenario_never_writes_actual_state compares the whole set of its fifty external import leaves against a reviewed inventory in both directions, refuses seven interior-mutability spellings and thirteen filesystem, clock, process and transport constructs as whole identifiers over every product file, and refuses the two mutable-borrow spellings as text, each with a control that requires the same reader to find those names in the workspace's own writer. every_declared_field_position_is_reviewed compares the whole set of its 153 declared field positions against a reviewed inventory in both directions and requires exactly the thirteen fields of the input struct to be public, so a field added anywhere in the package, in a module nobody predicted, spelling nothing anybody thought to forbid, fails as a position nobody reviewed. That same inventory is the exhaustive net behind section 22.4's no default recommendation score and behind section 22.3's no mastery delta, and the mastery vocabulary it is compared against is read out of P2-N2's own ladder.rs and academic-domain's own MasteryLevel rather than typed here, so a rung added there extends the guard without anybody editing the test. Every identifier, digest, seat, review aggregate and concept signal in its test tree is synthetic and built in process; no real record, catalogue or review is read and no network call is made. Its resolved link closure intersected with the socket-capable crates is exactly [libc], which reaches it through academic-domain and through academic-policy by way of academic-offering.
